3. The Investigating Officer of the Anti-Corruption Commission investigated the case and submitted his report before the Anti-Corruption Commission. Once the Anti-Corruption Commission accorded sanction under section 32 of the Act, the Investigating Officer submitted the charge sheet being Charge Sheet No. 284 dated 14-5-2008 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the Act and Rule 15 of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007. 

 4. After submission of the charge sheet by an order dated 18-5-2008, the same was accepted and cognizance was taken by the Court of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge and the case record was transmitted to the Court of Special Judge, No. 6, Dhaka and it was registered as Special Case No. 12 of 2008. Thereafter, when the matter was pending for charge hearing before the learned Special Judge, Court No. 6, Dhaka, the petitioner filed an application dated 7-12-2016 for resolving the dispute relating to expenditures filed by the petitioner in the light of the order of the Appellate Division dated 8-8-2010 passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.215 of 2009 as well as the order dated 14-1-2008 passed by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 54 of 2008 and the order dated 3-3-2011 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Revision No. 249 of 2011 before proceeding with the framing of charge. 

 6. Mr Moudud Ahmed, appeared in person and submitted that the act of framing charge of an offence being a judicial act of the Court operating to the prejudice of the alleged offender, the Court is required to perform this act judiciously and not arbitrarily or willfully on any assumption or conjecture. He further submitted that learned Special Judge, Special Judge Court No. 6, Dhaka being over enthusiastic and biased most illegally and arbitrarily has framed the charge against the petitioner without complying with the mandatory provision of law as laid down in section 242 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (the Code) as such the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. He further submitted that the High Court Division should have considered that the charge has been framed against the accused petitioner without reading out and explaining the charge to him and without affording him an opportunity to plead guilty or not guilty and that the framing of charge was thus in violation of section 242 of the Code. However, in his order dated 21-6-2017, the learned Judge has written that the charge was read over and explained to the accused petitioner and the accused petitioner pleaded not guilty and sought for trial, which is completely untrue. He further submitted that the High Court Division has failed to appreciate that the trial Court without applying its judicial mind rejected the application for time filed by the petitioner on the ground that a revisional application was pending before the High Court Division and proceeded with the framing of charge arbitrarily and charge has been framed against the accused-petitioner without giving him any opportunity to place his application for discharge filed under section 241 A of the Code. He further submitted that the High Court Division has committed error of law in not considering that in view of the facts and circumstances of the case the conduct of the learned Judge of the trial Court clearly shows that he was seemingly biased and he has framed charge against the accused petitioner most illegally and arbitrarily even after the petitioner expressed no confidence in him. He further submitted that the High Court Division should have considered that the order dated 21-6-2017 passed by the learned Special Judge, Court No. 6, Dhaka writing a completely untrue statement that “গঠিত অভিযোগ উপস্থিত আসামী ব্যারিষ্টার মওদুদ আহমেদকে পাঠ ও ব্যাখ্যা করে শুনানো হলে তিনি নিজেকে নির্দোষ দাবী করিয়া বিচার প্রার্থনা করে।” is unbecoming for him as a judicial officer who is duty bound to ensure justice and therefore he has committed gross illegality. He further submitted that the learned Court below deliberately and intentionally framed charge against the accused-petitioner without affording him an opportunity to have a full hearing on the discharge application filed under section 241A of the Code and ignoring the orders passed by both the Divisions of the Supreme Court. He further submitted that in passing the order dated 21-6-2017 framing charge based on untrue statements, the learned Special Judge, Court No. 6, Dhaka has committed miscarriage of justice. He further submitted that the High Court Division on the one hand has allowed the application of the petitioner to transfer the case by an order dated 25-7-2017 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 32982 of 2017 and on the other hand, although the grounds were the same, summarily rejected the other application of the petitioner filed against the order of framing charge by the order of the same date, i.e. 25-7-2017 passed in Criminal Revision No. 1865 of 2017. Therefore, the impugned order of the High Court Division is contradictory, inconsistent and mutually conflicting with the order passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 32982 of 2017 and as such not tenable in law. He further submitted that if the impugned order dated 25-7-2017 is not set aside the petitioner will be highly prejudiced and suffer irreparable loss and injury.
